'''Christopher Abell''' (11 November 1957<ref name=Debretts>Abell, Prof Christopher. In ''Debrett's People of Today 2012'' (accessed 15 January 2012) ''(subscription required)''</ref> – 26 October 2020<ref name=dept_obituary>{{citation |url=https://www.ch.cam.ac.uk/news/professor-chris-abell-frs-fmedsci-1957-2020 |title=Professor Chris Abell FRS, FMedSci (1957 - 2020) |publisher=Department of Chemistry, University of Cambridge |date=27 October 2020 |access-date=15 November 2020}}</ref>) was a British [[chemical biology|biological chemist]] who was a professor of biological chemistry at the [[Yusuf Hamied Department of Chemistry]] and Todd-Hamied Fellow of [[Christ's College, Cambridge]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://astx.com/about/scientific_advisory_board/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130407084006/http://astx.com/about/scientific_advisory_board/|url-status=dead|archive-date=7 April 2013|title=Scientific Advisory Board|date=7 April 2013}}</ref> On his 2016 election to the [[Royal Society]], Abell's research was described as having "changed the face of drug discovery."<ref>{{citation |url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2016/04/new-fellows-2016/ |title=50 leading scientists elected as Fellows of Royal Society  |date=29 April 2016 |access-date=2 September 2016 }}</ref>

==Education==
Abell was educated at [[St John's College, Cambridge]],<ref name=Debretts /> gaining a Bachelor of Arts degree in [[Natural Sciences (Cambridge)|Natural Sciences]] in 1979 followed by PhD<ref name=aphd>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of Cambridge|url=http://idiscover.lib.cam.ac.uk/primo-explore/fulldisplay?docid=44CAM_ALMA21428181990003606&context=L&vid=44CAM_PROD&search_scope=SCOP_CAM_ALL&tab=cam_lib_coll&lang=en_US|title=Polyketide biosynthesis|first= Christopher|last=Abell|date=1982|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.350039}}|website=lib.cam.ac.uk|oclc=59312458}}</ref> on the topic of [[polyketide]] biosynthesis for research supervised by James Staunton in 1982.<ref name=CV>{{citation |url=http://www-abell.ch.cam.ac.uk/abellgroup/cv/cv.html |title=Abell Group Home Page: Curriculum vitae: Professor Christopher Abell |access-date=15 January 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060925145219/http://www-abell.ch.cam.ac.uk/abellgroup/cv/cv.html |archive-date=25 September 2006 |url-status=bot: unknown }} (accessed 15 January 2013)</ref>

==Career and research==
Abell held a research fellowship in the laboratory of [[David E. Cane]] at [[Brown University]], [[Providence, Rhode Island|Providence]], USA, studying [[terpene]] biosynthesis (1982–83).<ref name=Debretts /><ref name=CV /> In 1984, Abell joined the department of chemistry of the University of Cambridge, successively holding the positions of demonstrator, lecturer and reader in chemical biology, and becoming professor in biological chemistry in 2002.<ref name=Debretts /><ref name=CV /> He held visiting professorships at the [[Australian National University]] in [[Canberra]], [[University of Santiago de Compostela]], [[University of Canterbury]], [[Christchurch]], and the [[Paul Sabatier University]], [[Toulouse]].<ref name=Debretts /><ref name=CV /><ref name=Astex>[http://www.astex-therapeutics.com/about/sab.php Astex Therapeutics: Scientific Advisors and Clinical Consultants] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110814042020/http://www.astex-therapeutics.com/about/sab.php |date=14 August 2011 }} (accessed 5 January 2009)</ref> He was a fellow of [[Christ's College, Cambridge]], from 1986;<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://issuu.com/christsalumni/docs/christsmag2019_sc_v5_web|title=Christ's College Magazine 2019|website=Issuu|language=en|access-date=2020-01-01|archive-date=18 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210518174529/https://issuu.com/christsalumni/docs/christsmag2019_sc_v5_web|url-status=dead}}</ref> and was the college's Todd-Hamied Fellow.<ref name=Christs>[http://www.christs.cam.ac.uk/college-life/people/fellows/ Christ's College, University of Cambridge: The Fellows of Christ's College] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130305100653/http://www.christs.cam.ac.uk/college-life/people/fellows/ |date=5 March 2013 }} (accessed 7 January 2013)</ref> In 2013 he was appointed the first director of [[postdoctoral]] affairs at the University of Cambridge,<ref>[http://www.cam.ac.uk/for-staff/appointments/new-senior-post-to-support-post-doc-community University of Cambridge: new senior post to support post-doc community] (accessed 28 November 2013)</ref> and in 2016 was appointed pro-vice-chancellor for research.

Abell published over 200 papers.<ref name=Debretts /> His research interests include [[vitamin]] and [[amino acid]] [[biosynthesis]] as targets for the [[drug design|rational design]] of [[antimicrobial]]s; [[Fragment-based lead discovery|fragment-based approaches]] to [[enzyme inhibition]]; bacterial and plant [[riboswitch]]es; reactions in microdroplets;<ref name=ange>{{cite journal|last1=Theberge|first1=Ashleigh B.|last2=Courtois|first2=Fabienne|last3=Schaerli|first3=Yolanda|last4=Fischlechner|first4=Martin|last5=Abell|first5=Chris|last6=Hollfelder|first6=Florian|last7=Huck|first7=Wilhelm T. S.|title=Microdroplets in Microfluidics: An Evolving Platform for Discoveries in Chemistry and Biology|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition|volume=49|issue=34|year=2010|pages=5846–5868|issn=1433-7851|doi=10.1002/anie.200906653|pmid= 20572214|s2cid=18609389 |url=https://eprints.soton.ac.uk/340192/2/__soton.ac.uk_ude_personalfiles_users_jks1m11_mydesktop_theberge_2010_microdroplets%2520in%2520microfluidics-an%2520evolving%2520platform%2520for%2520discoveries%2520in%2520chemistry%2520and%2520biology.pdf}}</ref> and biological [[nanotechnology]].<ref>[http://www.ch.cam.ac.uk/staff/ca.html University of Cambridge: Department of Chemistry: Professor Chris Abell] (accessed 5 January 2009)</ref> His former doctoral students include [[Shankar Balasubramanian]].<ref name=shankarphd/>

===Commercial ventures===
Abell was the co-founder of several companies. In 1999, he co-founded [[Astex|Astex Technology Ltd]], which uses fragment-based drug discovery technology to discover cancer therapeutics.<ref name=Debretts /><ref name=Astex /> In 2001, he co-founded Akubio, which developed [[biosensor]]s for detecting bacteria and viruses; it was acquired by Inverness Medical Innovations in 2008.<ref>[http://www.businessweekly.co.uk/biomedtech-/11002-recycled-cambridge-biosensor-technology-attracts-millions-in-investment Vargas L. Recycled Cambridge biosensor technology attracts millions in investment ''Business Weekly'' (27 August 2008)] (accessed 5 January 2009)</ref> In 2010, he co-founded [[Sphere Fluidics]] to develop microdroplet technology.<ref>[http://www.spherefluidics.com/news_2010.php Sphere Fluidics: 2010 News] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121118084242/http://www.spherefluidics.com/news_2010.php |date=18 November 2012 }} (accessed 7 January 2013)</ref> In 2012 he co-founded Aqdot, a company developing a new microencapsulation technology.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.businessweekly.co.uk/news/cambridge-torchbearers/farm-fame-cambridge%E2%80%99s-%E2%80%98cereal%E2%80%99-life-science-entrepreneur|title=From farm to fame, Cambridge's 'cereal' life science entrepreneur {{!}} Business Weekly {{!}} Technology News {{!}} Business news {{!}} Cambridge and the East of England|last=Quested|first=Tony|website=www.businessweekly.co.uk|access-date=2020-01-01}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In 1981, he married Katherine Abell, who worked with him at the department of chemistry in Cambridge; they had a son.<ref name=dept_obituary /><ref name=CV /><ref>{{citation |url=https://www.ch.cam.ac.uk/group/abell/people |title=The Abell Group: Group Members |publisher=Department of Chemistry, University of Cambridge |access-date=15 November 2020}}</ref> He died suddenly on 26 October 2020.<ref name=dept_obituary />

==Awards and honours==
His awards include the [[Imperial Chemical Industries]] (ICI) Prize in Organic Chemistry in 1992,<ref name=CV /> the [[Hickinbottom Award]] of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/HickinbottomAward/PreviousWinners.asp|title=RSC Hickinbottom Award Previous Winners|website=rsc.org|access-date=2020-01-01}}</ref> and a Yamada Science Foundation Award.<ref name=Debretts /><ref name=CV /> In 2008 he was the MIT Novartis Lecturer, and in 2011 was a BIC International Fellow at the University of Canterbury, Christchurch, New Zealand.<ref>[http://www.bic.canterbury.ac.nz/International%20Fellows.shtml International Fellows] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304035526/http://www.bic.canterbury.ac.nz/International%20Fellows.shtml |date=4 March 2016 }}, University of Canterbury – Christchurch. Retrieved 3 December 2013</ref> He was elected a [[Fellow of the Academy of Medical Sciences]] (FMedSci) in 2012<ref>[http://www.acmedsci.ac.uk/p109.html The Academy of Medical Sciences: Fellows: Newly elected fellows] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130927123531/http://www.acmedsci.ac.uk/p109.html |date=27 September 2013 }} (accessed 7 January 2013)</ref> and a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS) in 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://royalsociety.org/people/christopher-abell-12842/|title= Professor Christopher Abell Biography|publisher= Royal Society|access-date= 1 May 2016}}</ref>
